clue.text: Following short climb, one buzzing flying saucer

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references (p. 12 f.)

indicators.note: short tells you the word for climb loses its final letter

parts.note: a climb is a rise
a bee is an insect that buzzes

explanation.surface: After a brief ascent, somebody spots a humming UFO.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims RISE to RIS. The definition is playful: not an alien craft but the plastic disc thrown in parks, which spins through the air like a saucer.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful description: the plastic throwing disc is saucer-shaped and glides through the air.

clue.text: No stomach for catlike rage

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of a body, so the word for catlike loses its central letter

parts.note: a cat is furry, so furry describes something like a cat

explanation.surface: Someone lacks the guts for a feline sort of anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No stomach for' removes the central R of FURRY, a five-letter word whose middle is its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean violent anger.

clue.text: Holly and I almost allowed kiss

indicators.note: almost means the word for allowed stops one letter early

parts.note: let is the past tense of let, meaning permitted
X is the sign for a kiss at the end of a letter or text

explanation.surface: The speaker and a woman called Holly came close to being permitted a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital makes Holly look like a person; it is the tree. 'almost' shortens LET to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus name of the holly tree.

clue.text: Puzzle is live: Oscar's ahead of Romeo

indicators.note: ahead of places the playwright's name before the letter for Romeo

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright; Oscar's is his surname
Romeo is the word for R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A quiz is being broadcast, with contestant Oscar leading Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar and Romeo both look like NATO alphabet letters, but only Romeo is: Oscar is the writer Wilde. 'ahead of' fixes the order. 'Puzzle' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to baffle or perplex someone.

clue.text: Provide with source of income but die without being set up

parts.note: to die is to end, to come to a finish

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: w/o is a common written abbreviation for without

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to give a dependant an income, yet dies before becoming established.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being set up' turns WO, the shorthand w/o for without, into OW in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a person or institution money or property that yields a regular living.

clue.text: Leave, and return for wee chat

parts.note: to leave is to go

indicators.note: return means the word for wee comes back the other way

parts.note: wee and piss are both informal words for urine or urinating

explanation.surface: Someone pops out and comes back for a little chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' reads as Scottish for small, but here it is the lavatory sense. 'return' turns PISS into SSIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: idle talk between friends, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Ignore erroneous theologian

indicators.note: erroneous means wrong, so the letters of the first word are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to a mistaken religious scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erroneous' is the anagram indicator, working on 'Ignore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an early Christian scholar of Alexandria, one of the most influential church thinkers of the third century.

clue.text: Dog trained to pick sheep and run

indicators.note: trained means drilled into a new shape, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dog has been taught to select individual sheep and to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' is the anagram indicator; the pool is PICK SHEEP plus R, the cricket abbreviation for run.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small black tailless Belgian breed, once kept on canal barges.

clue.text: Preserve from oblivion each dog or cat you had

parts.note: per means each, as in ten pounds per head
a dog or a cat is a typical pet
U is text-message shorthand for you
had means ate, as in I had lunch

explanation.surface: Keep alive the memory of every dog or cat you ever owned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' looks like owning the animals; it is eating. U for 'you' is texting shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make something last so that it is not forgotten.

clue.text: Harry overawed as verdict overturned

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or ravage, so the letters of the next word are thrown about

explanation.surface: Prince Harry is stunned when a court ruling is reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is the verb, to harass, and signals the anagram of 'overawed'. 'overturned' belongs to the definition: the US Supreme Court struck this ruling down in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1973 US Supreme Court abortion ruling, struck down by the Dobbs decision in 2022.

clue.text: Some say where to curl up

indicators.note: some say signals that the word for where to is heard, not read

parts.note: whither is the old word meaning to what place

explanation.surface: A few people tell you the best spot to snuggle down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some say' is the homophone indicator: for speakers who do not sound the H, WHITHER and the answer are said alike. The 'to' belongs with 'where', not with 'curl up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of a leaf shrivelling and drying out.

clue.text: Strong drink in soldiers' quarters extremely deficient

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, and deficient says the word for the quarters lacks them

parts.note: barracks are the buildings where soldiers live

explanation.surface: The supply of hard liquor at the army camp is badly lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely deficient' takes the first and last letters, B and S, off BARRACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a potent Asian spirit distilled from palm sap, rice or molasses.

clue.text: Hippies fine with less important folk

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lower means of less rank or importance
folk are people

explanation.surface: Counterculture types get along well with humbler folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as 'on good terms', but it is only the pencil-grade abbreviation F.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the 1960s name for the peace-and-love counterculture, who wore blossoms as a symbol.

clue.text: Pass smashed into groin, making one grumpy

indicators.note: into says the jumbled pass goes inside the word for groin

parts.note: the crotch is the groin, where the legs meet

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters of pass are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football pass struck a player in the groin, leaving him in a foul mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The footballing scene hides an anatomical word: 'smashed' rearranges 'Pass' to SSPA, which goes 'into' the word for groin.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: an ill-tempered, irritable person.

clue.text: Misguidedly superintend removing page in contracts

indicators.note: misguidedly means led astray, so the letters are sent to the wrong places
removing says the letter for page is taken out of the long word first

explanation.surface: A manager wrongly oversees the removal of a page from legal agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes P out of SUPERINTEND, leaving SUERINTEND, which 'Misguidedly' anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: formal deeds binding one party to another, as an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Pulse of athlete taken by head

indicators.note: taken by says the athlete is joined by the word for head, which follows

parts.note: a runner is one kind of athlete
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: The head teacher checks an athlete's heart rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' is not a heartbeat but an edible seed of a pod-bearing plant. 'taken by' joins the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a legume, the common British climbing vegetable with long green pods.

clue.text: Gosh: black Briton addressed using slang

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils and in chess
limey is American slang for a British person, from the lime juice once issued to British sailors

explanation.surface: Good heavens: a black British man was spoken to in street slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a British exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Non-flyer's rival not delayed

indicators.note: not says the word for delayed is absent from the word for rival

parts.note: to rival is to emulate, to try to equal
delayed means late

explanation.surface: The competitor of a nervous traveller who refuses to fly was on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes LATE from EMULATE. 'rival' is a verb here, to try to match.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large Australian bird that cannot get off the ground.

clue.text: Getting on at school all the time

definitions.meaning: stepping onto a ship, train or plane
describes a pupil who lives at the school in term time instead of going home each day

explanation.surface: A pupil is said to be progressing well at school without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: embarking on a vessel, and living in at a residential school.

clue.text: Fat's limited appeal

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the word for fat loses its last letter

parts.note: suet is the hard fat from round the kidneys of cattle, used in British puddings

explanation.surface: Fatty food has only a narrow attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims the T from SUET. 'appeal' is a verb here, to petition.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym in the sense of petitioning: a defeated side might plead for peace.

clue.text: Infiltrating protest group, spot thief

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the word for spot enters the protest group

parts.note: a picket is a line of strikers or protesters outside a workplace
a pock is a spot or pustule on the skin

explanation.surface: Having slipped in among the demonstrators, someone identifies a robber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' reads as a verb, to notice, but it is a noun, a skin blemish; 'Infiltrating' sends it inside the line of strikers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a criminal who steals from people's clothing in crowds.

clue.text: Sophisticated early settlement a source of misery

parts.note: Ur was one of the earliest cities, in ancient Sumer, a crossword favourite
a bane is a cause of ruin or distress

explanation.surface: A refined early colony became a cause of suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: suave, polished and worldly in manner.

clue.text: After look round market at last, merchants go on together

definitions.note: write the first two words together and you get the name of the 1950s radio comedy troupe this actor belonged to

indicators.note: After says the merchants come after the look-and-letter piece
round says the word for look surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of market

parts.note: merchants are sellers of goods

explanation.surface: Having browsed the market, traders at closing time carry on side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a trick: 'go on' joined up gives Goon, and this actor starred in BBC radio's The Goon Show. 'round' and 'at last' build the first name; 'After' puts the surname second.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: he was a Goon, a star of the BBC radio comedy The Goon Show.

clue.text: Drunk workers organised to be replaced in plant in spring

indicators.note: replaced is read as re-placed: the union's letters are put back in a new position within the plant

parts.note: the tulip is a bulb that flowers in spring
organised workers form a trade union, abbreviated TU

explanation.surface: Tipsy labourers are due to be swapped out at the factory in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' is read as re-placed: the trade union's two letters leave the front of the flower and go back in after LI. The plant is not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: someone intoxicated is said to be this.

clue.text: Almost silent area in Parliament

indicators.note: almost means the word for silent stops one letter short

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak
A is the abbreviation for area, as in formulas

explanation.surface: A nearly noiseless corner of the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final letter of the word for silent. The assembly meant is Russia's, not Westminster's.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the lower house of the Russian national legislature.

clue.text: Inform Count William

definitions.meaning: to let someone know a piece of news
an old verb for reckoning up numbers, as when votes are counted
first name of the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: Somebody must let Count William know.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: to notify, to reckon up, and the surname of the Swiss folk hero.

clue.text: Woollen garment, black and light brown?

parts.note: tar is the black sticky stuff used on roads, and to tar something is to blacken it
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A knitted jumper in black and beige, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark allows for TAR standing loosely for black. The cloth is typically many-coloured, which the two sober colours hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The checked woollen cloth of the Scottish Highlands, and by extension a kilt or plaid made from it.

clue.text: Posture showing height and fitness different in one character

indicators.note: character here is a letter: the wanted word is one letter away from the words for height and for fitness

parts.note: height is altitude and fitness is aptitude, two words that themselves differ only in their second letter

explanation.surface: A pose that displays stature and health, each differently, in a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different in one character' means one letter changed: ALTITUDE (height) and APTITUDE (fitness) each become the answer when their second letter is swapped for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the way the body is held or positioned.

clue.text: Two erections in garden, one incomplete still

indicators.note: one incomplete says one of the two garden buildings is missing its last letter

parts.note: a hut is a small building put up in a garden
a shed is the other small garden building

explanation.surface: A pair of garden structures, one unfinished, remain standing even now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one incomplete' trims HUT, the first of the two garden buildings, to HU. 'still' is an adjective here, meaning quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: quiet, with all noise stopped.

clue.text: Back behind greedy type in queue

indicators.note: behind says the word for back is placed after the greedy type

parts.note: a pig is a glutton, a greedy person
the tail is the back or rear end of something

explanation.surface: Standing in line, someone has their back turned behind a glutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queue' is not a line of people: it is an old word, from the French for tail, for a plait of hair. 'behind' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Old synonym: a plait of hair hanging down the back of the head.
